title: Batman: Return of the Joker
blurb: Game Boy platformer. Hand-translated from the disassembly and verified bit-exact against the cartridge.

rom.file: Batman - Return of the Joker (USA, Europe).gb
rom.romNote: The file stays at the repo root this workflow -- 54 python tools carry the filename as a literal. Recorded here so a second cartridge knows to put its ROM beside a manifest instead.

display.frameHzNote: Game Boy DMG: 4194304 Hz / 70224 cycles per frame = 59.7275006. Derived, not rounded -- see docs/knowledge/07-clocks-and-framerates.md. NOTE THE DEVIATION: the shipped loop uses FRAME_MS = 1000/59.73 (src/main.js), a rounded rate worth 0.7 us per frame. Everything in the corpus was verified against that constant and it is NOT changed by this manifest -- the exact value is recorded here so the next game does not inherit the shortcut.

entryNote: boot(canvas, opts) is the host contract and its option names are still Batman-shaped ({level, title, ending, difficulty}). entries[] and options[] below are the generic shapes a later {entry, options} call will read; nothing converts between them yet.

input.note: Masks are the $FFE1/$FFE2 joypad bit layout read in the VBlank ISR at 0:$07CC-$07F6. They mirror BTN in src/player.js, and tests/registry.test.js asserts the two agree so this cannot drift.
input.keymapNote: Keys are matched on e.code (physical position), which is why KeyZ and KeyY are both B -- see src/input.js. src/input.js still owns the live table; this is the written-down copy the launcher reads masks through.

entries.label: Title screen
entries.note: The default. Any other value boots straight into that level and skips the title entirely.
Boss 3 — playable; one sky band sits a pixel off

entries.label: Ending
entries.note: 4 pictures, the credit crawl and THE END

entriesNote: Lifted verbatim from index.html's LEVEL_NOTE, INCLUDING the two sentinels: 0 = start at the title screen, 99 = watch the ending without beating the Joker. The per-level notes are measured status, not aspiration -- five of them were once FALSE for months, and the rule is that porting something means fixing its line.

options.label: Difficulty
options.note: $C756. The cartridge boots at 1 -- read off the real machine at gameplay start, not assumed. NOT cosmetic: 0 turns off water damage entirely and stretches level 1's water-spout pause from $10 to $50 frames, and 2 gives bosses +5 HP.

values.label: Easy — no water damage, slow spouts

charactersNote: DECLARED, WIRED TO NOTHING. The tile budget is the real constraint on ever having two protagonists on screen: the DMG shares 256 OBJ tiles, the player owns a fixed 12 ($00-$0B) streamed four per frame on a three-column ring, and the streamer's cursor is READ BACK by the pose selector as a repaint-in-flight gate (src/render/metasprite.js). This is here so a borrow system can reason before it loads a single module.

characters.label: Batman
characters.tileBudgetNote: OBJ tiles $00-$0B, streamed one 4-tile column per frame (sub_00_2C13), so a changed pose takes 3 frames to fully repaint.

enemiesNote: DECLARED, WIRED TO NOTHING. One entry per driver state (loc_01_50C3, table 1:$50D3, indexed on state-1). `module` names the file Phase 9 of the restructure will create; today every one of them still lives in src/enemies.js. They are written down now so the split has to produce one file per unit rather than a single bosses.js.
